summary: A statement from the Internet Architecture Board arguing that changing the addresses of hosts and subnets, called renumbering, will become more common, so solutions that make it easier should be developed and deployed. It also touches on how DNS names relate to IP addresses.

eli5.summary: When a family moves, every friend must learn the new address. This note says moving should be made much easier for computers on the network, because it will happen more often.

questions: why use domain names instead of ip addresses
what did the iab recommend about renumbering
subtitle: The IAB warns that changing IP addresses will get more common and asks for tools and habits that make it easier.

tldr.problem: Renumbering, meaning changing the IP addressing information of hosts and subnets, is costly, tedious and error-prone, yet it is likely to become more widespread.
tldr.mechanism: The IAB recommends using Fully Qualified Domain Names instead of IP addresses in configuration, avoiding hardcoded addresses and address-based licensing, and building a toolkit around DHCP, router discovery, service location and secure dynamic DNS updates.
tldr.outcome: It is an advisory statement, not a standard. It also asks that renumbering experience be shared and documented, and welcomes the PIER working group.

today: RFC 1900 is an Informational statement from the IAB (February 1996), and the metadata shows no RFC obsoleting or updating it. It is advice from its time, so its mentions of work in progress reflect the state of 1996.

sections.title: Why Renumbering Will Happen
sections.content:
Renumbering is a change in the IP addressing information of a host or subnet. The RFC gives three examples: moving a host to another subnet, splitting a subnet that is overloaded, and an organization changing its addressing plan.

Organizations that need Internet-wide connectivity but do not provide enough address aggregation will increasingly have to renumber. With current technology, extended deployment of Classless Inter-Domain Routing (CIDR) is vital, so such organizations use addresses from a block allocated to their service provider. When they change provider, their addresses must change to contain routing information growth. If they do not renumber, the consequences may include limited IP connectivity or extra cost for providers, or both.

Today, renumbering is usually costly, tedious and error-prone, tools are few and little deployed, and there is little documentation or shared experience.
sections.eli5: If you change internet company, your computers may have to change their addresses too, and right now that is a slow, messy job.

sections.title: Names Versus Addresses
sections.content:
An individual host is identified by the IP addresses on its interfaces. The Domain Name System (DNS) gives legible names to those addresses, and its name space is independent of the IP address space. A change of DNS name may signal a real change of function or ownership, whereas a change of IP address is a purely technical event.

Using domain names defers the binding between an entity and its address until run time. Fully Qualified Domain Names (see RFC 1594) are expected to be longer lived than IP addresses, and relying on them confines the changes needed for renumbering to the DNS. Where addresses and names of desktop or portable systems are both allocated dynamically, only a highly responsive dynamic DNS update mechanism can cope.
sections.eli5: A person's name stays the same when they move house. DNS lets computers use the name and look up the current address.

sections.title: The IAB Recommendations
sections.content:
The IAB strongly recommends that designs and implementations minimize the cases where IP addresses are stored in non-volatile storage maintained by humans, such as configuration files. Configuration should use FQDNs whenever possible, hardcoding addresses in applications should be deprecated, and name-to-address files other than DNS configuration should be avoided. For legacy applications that need addresses, the configuration file should be generated automatically from a file of domain names, with addresses filled in by DNS lookup. Licensing technology based on a host's IP address makes renumbering hard and should be strongly discouraged.

A toolkit to automate host renumbering is essential. The Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP) is clearly an essential part of it, along with dynamic router discovery (RFC 1256), service location, and authenticated dynamic DNS updates. The goal is truly autoconfigurable TCP/IP hosts.

The IAB also encourages sharing and documenting renumbering experience, suggests the IETF Operational Requirements Area as the place for it, and welcomes the PIER (Procedures for Internet and Enterprise Renumbering) working group.
sections.eli5: Write down names, not numbers, and let computers get their numbers automatically. Then moving house is easy.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The RFC says renumbering is believed to be compatible with the Internet security architecture, as long as addresses do not change during the lifetime of a security association. It adds nothing further on security.
sections.eli5: Changing addresses is safe as long as it does not happen in the middle of a protected conversation.
